solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decorated old men on opposite sides at Waterloo died

parts.words: old men on opposite sides at Waterloo
parts.note: two words for father, one from each side of the battle: English PA and French PERE
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A veteran recalls a medal-winning soldier from the Battle of Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is slang for father; Waterloo set the English against the French, so one father is PA and the other the French PERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that has been papered has been given wallpaper, one way of decorating it.

clue.text: Foreign issue of public relations "bible" getting its approval?

parts.note: PR is public relations
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
da is Russian for yes, the approval of the paper's own country

explanation.surface: A PR firm's handbook seeking its own approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers to the definition: the Russian paper's own language says DA for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pravda was the official Soviet newspaper, so an issue printed abroad in Russian.

clue.text: A little exercise before Kitty gets up

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: gets up in a down clue means the word rises, read from bottom to top

parts.note: puss is a cat, a kitty

explanation.surface: A spot of exercise before the cat wakes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' turns PUSS upwards into SSUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up, called a push-up in America, is a single floor exercise raising the body by the arms.

clue.text: Marble game popular with a number of spectators

parts.note: RU is rugby union
in means fashionable, popular
the gate is the attendance at a sporting event

explanation.surface: A game of marbles that draws a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruin agate is a banded agate whose pattern looks like ruins; an agate is also a playing marble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin agate is a decorative stone, and agates were the prized glass or stone marbles in children's games.

clue.text: Pulling motion creating pain in the neck

definitions.meaning: the act of hauling something along

explanation.surface: A dragging movement that leaves a crick in the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag means both a pull along the ground and, informally, a bore or annoyance.

clue.text: Horseman protecting lord repelled villain

indicators.note: protecting means the outer word wraps round and shields the inner one

parts.note: a horseman is a rider

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A mounted bodyguard shielding a nobleman fends off some scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' reverses the lord's abbreviation before it goes in. The villain is from Batman, not a generic crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riddler is one of Batman's best-known adversaries, a comic-book bad guy who leaves puzzles at his crimes.

clue.text: Wild, noisy drummer, ultimately one for a band

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word drummer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
pro means in favour of, for
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A rowdy drummer finally joining a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild, noisy drummer' reads as one description; the definition is just the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rip-roaring means boisterous and exuberant, both unrestrained and loud.

clue.text: Spaniard possibly to pass on turn

parts.note: to pass on is to die
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A Spaniard might pass when it is his turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a common Spanish first name, so a Spaniard possibly bears it.

clue.text: Hail not unusual in Scottish region

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters set out in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Hail is not a rarity in this part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges HAILNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothian is the area of Scotland around Edinburgh, a historic county and council region.

clue.text: Awfully poor mistake getting in the red

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so this word goes inside the other

parts.note: ruby is the colour red
bish is British slang for a mistake

explanation.surface: A bad error that leaves the accounts in the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' suggests debt; red is the colour ruby.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbishy means worthless or shoddy, of very poor quality.

clue.text: Cunningly multiplied by two a nice prime number

indicators.note: cunningly says the letters are craftily rearranged

parts.note: the little word a, multiplied by two, gives two copies of the letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle: doubling something to reach a nice prime number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'multiplied by two' turns A into AA; with NICE PRIME that gives eleven letters for 'Cunningly' to rearrange. 'Number' is the crossword sense: a song.
explanation.definitionFit: American Pie is Don McLean's 1971 hit song, and in crosswords a song or musical piece is a number.

clue.text: VAT reduction in train

indicators.note: reduction in says the word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground, whose trains are called tubes

explanation.surface: A cut in Value Added Tax, the British sales tax, on rail travel.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like Value Added Tax, the British sales tax, but it is the definition: a large vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large container for liquids, and a tub is a similar open vessel.

clue.text: Might associated with underworld boss causing alarm

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
may and might are both verbs of possibility

explanation.surface: A powerful mob boss's might spreads fear through the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster; here it is Dis, ruler of the Roman land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of shock and distress, close in meaning to alarm as a noun.

clue.text: Revealing costume: nothing stops brother wearing one

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so this letter sits inside the word for brother

parts.note: a monk is a brother in a religious order
O, the figure zero, means nothing
wearing a coat is being in it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A skimpy swimsuit: nothing stops a friar from putting one on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' is a monk, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A monokini is a topless bikini bottom or one-piece cut-out swimsuit, a very skimpy outfit for the beach.

clue.text: Germ gets in badly preserved root

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A germ gets into a poorly pickled root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges GERMGETSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is the young underground stem of ginger kept in syrup, a candied rhizome.

clue.text: Sock someone draped around queen's cocktail

indicators.note: draped around means the outer phrase is hung around the inner piece

parts.note: to sock someone is to plant a punch on them
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; with the possessive S it gives ERS

explanation.surface: Hitting someone who has draped themselves over the Queen's shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock someone' is to plant a punch, read without the a; 'draped around' sets the Queen's initials and S inside that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Planter's punch is a rum-based mixed drink from the Caribbean, a classic cocktail.

clue.text: Pastime that's welcome, occupying page in recent Times

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space, so the greeting goes inside

parts.note: lately means in recent times
hi is a greeting, a welcome

explanation.surface: A hobby that is welcome, filling a page in recent issues of The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts the greeting inside the rest. Capital T on 'Times' points to the newspaper, but it just means recent times.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is stamp collecting, a popular hobby.

clue.text: British ready for some loud shows of affection?

definitions.meaning: ready is slang for cash, and ... is British slang for pounds

explanation.surface: Some British people are always ready for loud displays of fondness.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackers means both pounds in British slang and loud smacking kisses.

clue.text: Planning part of Michaelmas term in Dingwall

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Planning to spend the autumn term in Dingwall, a small town in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterminding a scheme is planning and directing it, the organising brain behind it.

clue.text: Foul initially seen as being over the top

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above, earlier in the answer
initially picks the first letter of seen

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as being
a lid is a top

explanation.surface: A foul initially seen as going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the top' looks like one phrase meaning excessive; split, it places pieces above LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid means filthy and wretched, so it is a synonym of foul.

clue.text: Pay individually — split other half?

parts.note: to split is to leave, to go
Dutch is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, from 'Duchess of Fife'

explanation.surface: Pay separately, sharing the bill with your partner?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' suggests dividing the bill; it is leaving. 'My old Dutch' is a London Cockney term for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is to have each person pay for their own share, as on a date.

clue.text: No point going back for old English preacher

indicators.note: going back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
the nub is the central point

explanation.surface: An old English preacher with no reason to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns NAYNUB into BUNYAN.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan was a seventeenth-century English Puritan preacher, author of The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: One spot on about force of old religious image

indicators.note: on means placed after, so these pieces follow the rest

parts.note: C is circa, about
the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was the old police force of Northern Ireland
I is the Roman numeral one
a spot is a fix, a tight situation

explanation.surface: Someone right about a former force finds an old religious picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot on' looks like one phrase meaning exactly right; it splits, with 'on' meaning placed after. The Royal Ulster Constabulary was Northern Ireland's police until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ, a devotional image in Christian worship.

clue.text: Tavern has appeal, would you not agree?

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: The pub has charm, doesn't it?
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is British slang contraction of isn't it, a tag question seeking agreement.

clue.text: Carriage lined at the front with gold

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of the word lined

parts.note: with and and both join things together
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A coach lined at the front with gold leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with a folding top, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Rome's increasingly spoilt, at first, for choice of popes?

parts.note: più is Italian for more, as in the musical direction più mosso

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of spoilt

explanation.surface: Rome increasingly spoilt for choice when electing popes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pius was the papal name taken by twelve popes, hence a popular choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Pius is a papal name chosen by many popes, making it a favourite selection.

clue.text: Length of old Henry's skipping torment!

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: hell is torment
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Old Henry VIII, pressing on despite the agony of torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' suggests a king; here it is the electrical unit, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell was an old measure of cloth, about 45 inches, used before metric units.

clue.text: I left data lying around, moderately carelessly

indicators.note: lying around means turned round, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
gently means in a moderate, mild way

explanation.surface: An admission of leaving papers about, somewhat thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying around' turns I L GEN into NEGLI.
explanation.definitionFit: To act negligently is to act without proper care, which is acting carelessly.

clue.text: Person calming down someone after match in Kent?

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE
a dater is someone looking for a romantic match

explanation.surface: A dating hopeful in Kent, settling down after a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England. 'Match' looks like a game; it is the dating sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedater is someone who sedates, giving a drug or treatment that soothes a patient.

clue.text: Advice from "mother" for one wife and female

parts.note: say means for example, for one
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A mother's wisdom, as given to one wife and woman.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'be mother' is British for pouring the tea or drinks; the pourer asks guests to say when to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Say when' is what someone pouring a drink tells you, asking you to signal when there is enough.
